juno: Heads-up — onboarding orca50k-int4 (50k ctx). We see nondeterministic drift after a forced KV shard eviction during a deep prefill. Different flavor from prior reports: the stitch discontinuity seems correlated with our compressed-kv format (we pack per-key metadata) rather than pure compute rounding.

sachin: Can you paste a repro + minimal logs?

juno: Repro command (deterministic):
```bash
./eval-driver --model orca50k-int4 --seed 2026 --prompt tests/deep_prefill_50k.txt --prefill 46000 --evict-token 2048 --max-tokens 256
```

juno: Short log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-29T10:12:01Z] kv_shard=5 kv_idx=65528 ropescale=1.000074 meta_crc=0x9f3a
[2026-03-29T10:12:01Z] kv_shard=6 kv_idx=0     ropescale=0.999538 meta_crc=0x9f3b  <-- scale mismatch after restore + metadata change
[2026-03-29T10:12:02Z] token_delta=0.31 regen_nll=+16.4%
```

lee: Interesting — the meta_crc flips when we recompute and reserialize the compressed kv block. Might be a different serializer ordering for int4 path producing different ropescale writes.

sachin: So hypothesis: when we evict a shard we later reconstruct it and write back KV with per-key metadata including ropescale estimates. The int4 serialization path quantizes and packs floats differently, so ropescale stored on-disk differs slightly from runtime recompute, causing stitch mismatch.

juno: Confirmed: disabling compressed-kv storage (fallback to raw keys) makes the drift vanish. Also observed that if we persist the ropescale explicitly in the KV header and read it back (instead of recomputing), continuity is preserved.

lee: Proposal: persist a canonical ropescale value in the KV shard header at eviction time and use that canonical value on restore (avoid recompute-on-restore for int4 fused kernels). Also add a CRC check and a debug flag to fail-on-mismatch in onboarding runs.

sachin: I like persisting the canonical scale — that avoids per-shard rounding divergences. We should also ensure we keep a tiny epsilon reconciliation step if header missing (backwards compat).

juno: Drafted PR #4201: "kv: persist canonical ropescale in shard header to avoid recompute drift (int4/compressed-kv)". Includes tests/unit/test_kv_persist_ropescale.py and an integration reproducer tests/integration/evict_restore_orca50k.toml.

ci-bot: canary/orca50k reported regen drift exceed threshold at 2026-03-29T10:15:00Z; canary paused.

lee: Running a small 5-seed smoke patched vs unpatched on p4d. Command:
```bash
./scripts/smoke_longprefill.sh --model orca50k-int4 --pr 4201 --seeds 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 --prefill 47000 --evict-token 512 --out /tmp/orca50k-smoke-3100000001
```

juno: Great — also add an onboarding CI gate: if a model onboarding run with prefill+evict scenario sees regen drift >1% we fail. For orca50k, threshold for this experiment should be 0.5% given large context sensitivity.

sachin: Note: we should backfill the runtime reader to accept legacy shards without header (compute fallback), but log a telemetry metric so we can detect prevalence.

lee: Early smoke results: patched run shows ropescale continuity within 1.8e-5, regen NLL back to baseline across seeds. Uploading logs to s3://redwood-ci/orca50k/3100000001/smoke_logs.tar.gz

ci-bot: queued canary create for orca50k-int4 with PR #4201.

juno: Next steps: (1) full 20-seed eval on stage dedicated, (2) backport to dedicated/runtime and compressed-kv serializer, (3) add onboarding gate and failing debug flag in CI, (4) roll canary once full eval clean.

sachin: I'll review PR and add the fallback header compatibility + telemetry.

deploy-bot: Canary create request queued for orca50k-int4 with PR #4201.

juno: Thanks all — will follow up with the full eval artifacts. :thumbsup:
